newsitem.title: CROATIA: Bank Austria plans to expand in Croatia.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria plans to expand in Croatia.

text.p: Bank Austria officially opened the new offices of its Croatian subsidiary on Wednesday and announced plans to enlarge its network and offer new services in the country.
The bank and its investment banking arm want to become market leaders among foreign financial institutions present in Croatia, top officials told a news conference here.
Bank Austria Croatia will open a representative office in Dubrovnik on the Adriatic coast later today.
It aims to set up branches in Rijeka and Dubrovnik before the end of this year, its director Anton Knett said.
Since launching its operations in the centre of the capital in mid-April, the bank has taken 15 million kuna in giro accounts and savings deposits, he said.
Its balance sheet was expected to grow to around 500 million kuna by the end of 1997.
It is mulling plans to raise 100 million kuna through a bond denominated in the Croatian currency in the next few months, said another bank official who declined other details.

The bank's investment unit is also gearing up to take its share of Croatia's growing capital market. It is waiting for a brokerage licence from the securities commission, head of Investmentbank Austria Helmut Horvath told Reuters.
"We specialise in corporate support in restructuring and acquisitions, but also offer a range of other sevices from advisory to listing and further financing," he said.

After acting as co-lead manager in the public offering of shares in Croatia's leading pharmaceutical company Pliva, IB Austria wants to take an active interest in sell-offs of remaining state firms such as large utilities.
Horvath also mentioned plans to set up an investment fund which will assume a role in the upcoming voucher privatisation of remaining state assets in smaller and medium-sized companies.
The proposed scheme, designed to divest some 16-18 billion kuna worth of holdings, is set to begin in autumn.
